body:
this likely makes sense, but I wonder if we should have this condition only if InstantSearch is already unmounted?

It makes sense also to keep the length in all cases, even when we later expose pushState to different routers (for eg. vue router), as they would behave the same.

Just leaving this as a possibility, I think it makes sense to check in all cases

If people elect to use the history router for IS, I think it's ok if our behaviour takes precedence during the lifecycle of InstantSearch.

For that, I agree we could only check the history length if `dispose()` has been called, so we're not losing state to url sync.

yes, agreed, we probably want to enforce this bail out only happens after dispose. Maybe the condition could be rolled into the the shouldPushState value?

```
dispose() 
  this.shouldPushState = this.shouldPushState && this.lastHistoryLength === window.history.length
```

something like that maybe?
This is nitpicking, so feel free to leave it as is. There are no mentions related to subscription other than here, and I wonder if `this.isDisposed` wouldn't be more appropriate here.
I was thinking that isDisposed sounds like a negative condition, but it's actually what we want to know in the later condition, so it can make sense that way too
I'll make the update, thanks for the suggestion!

It's already initialized in L84.

```suggestion
```

**suggestion (non-blocking):** "Last" implies nothing will follow, "latest" means "most recent".

I'm not 100% sold on the name as it doesn't convey that this is a counter of our changes to the history stack, but I don't have anything better to suggest. Since it's private and the comment gives more context we can probably leave it.

```suggestion
  private latestHistoryLength: number = 0;
```

body:
Do we have a test the assets the following flow:

```
start InstantSearch
make some changes (url changes)
dispose
try to make changes (not possible)
start InstantSearch again
make changes (url changes)
```

I'm assuming the router gets recreated on the next start of InstantSearch, but not 100% sure. Do you know?

**suggestion (non-blocking):** I find this statement (`!this.isDisposed || this.lastHistoryLength === window.history.length`) hard to grasp inlined like that, behavior isn't obvious (why only one is required). Could we move it to its own variable so the behavior has a name, and comment it as a whole?

**question (non-blocking):** if I understand correctly, this is meant to mimic a third-party router behavior which would switch page, triggering a `search.dispose()` as a side-effect in some `componentWillUnmount`-like lifecycle, correct?

If yes, could we make this a local function to make it obvious (e.g., `navigateToOtherPage(page)`)?

**suggestion (non-blocking):** same comment as `src/lib/__tests__/routing/spa-test.ts`, we could abstract this behavior to make it clearer when reading the tests, and accept a callback to perform the in-between assertions.

**question (non-blocking):** to be fully clear, this is the behavior we want to document (third-party router did initiate a navigation but wrote later, so we can't "escape" an in-between write), correct?
**suggestion (non-blocking):** same comment as in `src/lib/__tests__/routing/spa-test.ts`.
**question:** Why is this commented? It does affect the test output.

**question:** If I understand correctly, this is the use case when a third-party router uses `replaceState` instead of `pushState`, so the history length didn't change (but `dispose` was called), therefore we can't prevent a write on our end.

So the URL is cleaned in this case (contrary to what the test description says), isn't it?
**question:** Is it actually debounced?

**question:** The only difference I see between this test and the one in `src/lib/__tests__/routing/spa-test.ts` is that there's no intermediary `dispose()`. What use case does this represent? We might need a comment (and/or change the test description) to make it clear for later reading.

previousHistoryLength could also work.

Note that it's not *our* counter, but a counter by the browser `window.history.length`
